title: Speculative Tool Hedging & Schema-Aware Streaming — PRD (Draft)
content:
Purpose: draft a pragmatic feature set combining speculative (hedged) tool invocations with schema-aware incremental streaming so client SDKs can offer lower-latency, more deterministic UXs while preserving reproducibility and observability.

Background and problem statement:
- Hosted API customers build interactive flows that frequently call external tools (search, DB, code-exec). Tool latency is highly variable and dominates end-to-end response time for many UXs.
- Current streaming behavior holds back token emission until tool results arrive (blocking) or emits generic placeholders (uninformative).
- Developers want both low latency and stable, reproducible outputs: ad-hoc speculation by model/clients causes non-determinism, debugging complexity, and tangles telemetry.

Core idea (short):
Introduce a server-driven speculative tooling layer and a small set of streaming primitives (commit markers, variant envelopes, schema-delta frames) plus an SDK reconciliation contract. The runtime may issue low-cost speculative tool calls (hedgelets) in parallel and stream provisional structured fragments with an attached confidence envelope and provenance. Clients can render provisional UI and later reconcile to a committed canonical result using a deterministic merge rule.

Goals (what success looks like):
- 30–50% median tail latency reduction for tool-dependent streaming sessions in our battleground benchmarks.
- Deterministic reconciliation semantics: given same request+seed, server + SDK merge rule produce identical final transcript regardless of hedging or network reorder.
- Minimal SDK surface area: ergonomic primitives that are easy to adopt in mobile/web clients.
- Observability: per-fragment provenance, hedging telemetry, and automatic regression detection in Optimize.

Non-goals / out of scope:
- Full transactionality across multi-tool sagas (we defer to Dedicated for multi-step durable sagas).
- Arbitrary speculative writes to customer data stores (no speculative commits to customer DBs).

Terminology (introduced):
- Hedgelet: a speculative tool invocation executed at reduced cost/timeout (e.g., search with 50ms budget, truncated results). Hedgelets are tagged and never write external state.
- Schema-envelope: metadata attached to streamed fragments describing expected structured schema, confidence, and a content-hash.
- Commit marker: an explicit stream event indicating the server has confirmed/committed a fragment as canonical.
- Variant frame: when multiple speculative fragments exist for same logical slot, frames carry a variant-id and provenance.

User stories / examples:
1) Knowledge assistant: user asks "Summarize latest PR comments and highlight blockers." Model needs quick search over PR comments. Use hedgelets to fetch top-2 snippets; stream a provisional summary within 180ms using hedgelet results; once the full search completes, emit commit markers and reconcile; UI shows provisional summary with subtle badge until final commit.
2) Code runner: small function execution may be slow. Server hedges with a cached micro-run and streams a provisional result with confidence 0.6, later replaces with commit when the full-run completes.

API / streaming primitives (proposal):
- StreamEvent types (new): PROVISIONAL_FRAGMENT, VARIANT_FRAGMENT, COMMIT_MARKER, REORG_NOTICE.
- PROVISIONAL_FRAGMENT payload: text | structured-json-string, schema-envelope, fragment-id, variant-id, confidence (0.0-1.0), provenance-tags (["hedgelet:search-v1:50ms"]).
- COMMIT_MARKER payload: fragment-id, canonical-hash, reason ("tool-returned", "model-validated"), timestamp.
- REORG_NOTICE payload: list of fragment-id replacements and deterministic-merge-hint.

Deterministic reconciliation rules (SDK contract):
- Each provisional/variant includes content-hash and deterministic-merge-key (logical slot id).
- When COMMIT_MARKER for slot arrives, SDK will replace the slot atomically using the canonical-hash; if a REORG_NOTICE arrives, SDK applies merge hints in order (server supplies deterministic-merge-hint to resolve ordering).
- If commit never arrives within session TTL, SDK can either keep highest-confidence provisional or show a non-committed state per app policy.

SDK ergonomics (surface + examples):
- Minimal primitives: onFragment(fragment) -> Fragment object (id, content, confidence, provisional boolean, applyCommit(commitMarker) -> void).
- High-level widget: DeclarativeFragment(slotId, renderProvisional=true, fallbackMode="keep-provisional"|"hide"|"show-placeholder").
- Sample pseudo-code (JS):
  const stream = client.streamCompletion({prompt, enableSpeculativeTooling: true});
  stream.on('fragment', (f) => renderFragment(f));
  stream.on('commit', (c) => applyCommitToSlot(c.fragmentId));
  stream.on('reorg', (r) => applyReorgHints(r));
- SDK will expose stable hooks for telemetry: hedging.trace(hedgeletId, latencyMs, outcome), fragment.trace(fragmentId, confidence, replaced).

Server-side heuristics (runtime):
- Hedge policy config per-model-profile: e.g., hedgeMaxParallel=2, hedgeBudgetSlots=[0.05, 0.2] (fraction of allowed model time consumed for hedging), allowedToolSet for hedgelets.
- Hedge scoring: merge preliminary results by signal-weighting (provenance, cache-hit, model confidence) to produce a provisional fragment.
- Safety: hedgelets forbidden from executing state-mutating tool calls. All hedgelets run in a restricted role.

Structured output handling:
- Schema-envelope includes: declared schema-id (optional), minimal typing hints (string/array/object), and a small diff-format for incremental updates (line-based JSONL diffs).
- Server streams schema-deltas to enable clients to validate and show partial structured tables/lists.
- Commit events include final schema version and checksum so downstream evaluators can assert correctness.

Observability & Optimize integration:
- Telemetry events: HEDGELET_START, HEDGELET_END, HEDGELET_OUTCOME (hit/miss), FRAGMENT_EMITTED, COMMIT_EMITTED, REORG_OCCURRED. Events include latency, tool-id, and confidence.
- Optimize will surface: hedged vs unhedged latency delta, per-tool hedging ROI, and regression alerts when reconciliation flips > X% of provisional fragments.

Backward compatibility and fallbacks:
- Existing streaming clients that ignore new event types will still receive raw text content in order; provisional fragments are valid text blocks. COMMIT_MARKER is an additive event; clients that don't parse it will see the final canonical text when it is emitted as additional tokens.
- We will provide a server-side compatibility flag (speculative_off) to disable hedging per project/route.

Security & compliance constraints:
- Hedgelets cannot access PII-sensitive connectors unless the customer explicitly opts in and accepts non-durability.
- All hedgelet calls logged with provenance; logs are retained per customer retention policy.

Acceptance criteria / success metrics (detailed):
- Latency: 40% reduction in 95th percentile for the "search + summarize" benchmark in synthetic tests.
- Correctness: reconciliation mismatch rate < 2% in recorded field tests (i.e., cases where provisional content held and final commit differs in semantically important ways).
- SDK adoption: provide JS + mobile SDK prototypes; internal infra teams adopt in 2 pilot customers by end of Q2.

Implementation plan / milestones (quarterly):
- Week 0–4: API wireframes + server hedging control plane (flags + simple policy).
- Week 5–10: Runtime hedgelets plumbing + restricted tool runner + provisional fragment emission.
- Week 11–16: SDK primitives + sample web widget + telemetry hooks.
- Week 17–22: Pilot with 2 internal apps (Search-assistant, PR-summarizer).
- Week 23–30: Iterate on merge heuristics, expose policy tuning in Console, and Optimize dashboards.

Risks and mitigations:
- User confusion around provisional UI: mitigate with clear ephemeral badges and deliberate defaults (renderProvisional=false in critical flows).
- Cost: hedging increases tool calls; guardrail with per-route hedging budget and ROI telemetry in Optimize.
- Non-determinism: ensure deterministic-merge-hints and inclusion of content-hash in every frame; enforce deterministic ordering on server.

Open questions (to decide):
- Should hedgelets be billed at reduced unit price? (Ops + biz decision)
- Exact format for schema-deltas: JSON patch vs line-diff. JSON patch easier to reason about, diffs cheaper to stream.
- UI patterns: default install shows provisional badge vs default hides provisional fragments in conservative mode.

Appendix: quick sketch of transport examples (textual):
- Example stream (simplified):
  PROVISIONAL_FRAGMENT {slot: "summary:1", fragment-id: "f-123", variant: "h1", confidence: 0.45, content: "Draft: PR changes include X, Y...", provenance: ["hedgelet:search-v1:50ms"] }
  PROVISIONAL_FRAGMENT {slot: "summary:1", fragment-id: "f-124", variant: "h2", confidence: 0.33, content: "Also: tests failing in module Z...", provenance: ["cached-snippet:pr-987"] }
  COMMIT_MARKER {fragment-id: "f-125", slot: "summary:1", canonical-hash: "sha256:...", reason: "tool-returned"}
  REORG_NOTICE {replacements: [{from: "f-123", to: "f-125", hint: "append"}]}

Notes / next steps:
- Align with infra/serving-runtime on hedging resource costs and kernel-level limits.
- Product to prototype JS + Swift + Kotlin SDK samples and an internal Playbook for when to turn on speculative tooling.
- Legal to review retention and provenance disclosures for hedgelet logs.
